query: How should we define condition-number-style metrics for practical invertibility, and how predictive are they for inversion failure across tightly localized, diffuse, overlapping, and separated components?

response.query: How should we define condition-number-style metrics for practical invertibility, and how predictive are they for inversion failure across tightly localized, diffuse, overlapping, and separated components?
response.answer: Condition-number-style metrics assess invertibility by measuring the sensitivity of a system to perturbations; higher condition numbers indicate greater risk of inversion failure, especially for localized, diffuse, overlapping, and separated components. Predictive accuracy depends on the specific system and its inherent noise levels.

results.title: Set - Definition, Meaning & Synonyms
results.content: A *set* is a group of things that belong together, like the *set* of even numbers (2,4,6…) or the bed, nightstands, and dresser that make up your bedroom *set*. *Set* has many different meanings. To set in stone is to make permanent. put into place or position. place down, put down, set down. place (something) where one cannot find it again. set down according to a plan:"a carefully laid table with places set for four people". a set of twenty members. a set with 3 times 20 members. a set of one or more synonyms. the set of all points or lines that satisfy or are determined by specific conditions. set to a certain pitch. synonyms:  fix, gear up, prepare, ready, set up. synonyms:  lay out, set up. regulate or set the time of. regulate (a radio or television set) in order to receive a certain station or program. set to a certain position or cause to operate correctly. ### Vocabulary lists containing **set**.

results.title: Quantitative Phase Imaging XII, Conference Details
results.content: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) of live-cells delivers improved label-free contrast and enhanced cell phenotype analysis; however, live-cell QPI is difficult for many biologists to implement due to the complexity and limited throughput of current QPI based approaches. Quantitative phase imaging (QPI), and its three-dimensional analogue, holotomography, permit label-free measurements of the biophysical state of single cells with extreme precision. Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) is a vital technique in biology and medicine, enabling label-free microscopic analysis of living cells and transparent specimens. The classification or segmentation of cells from quantitative phase imaging (QPI) measurements enables studies of cell function and behavior, disease progression and prognosis, high-throughput and automated analyses, and drug development. Label-free high-content analysis at the single cell level utilizing artificial neural network supported correlative bright field imaging and digital holographic quantitative phase microscopy. This work presents a comprehensive approach to quantitative, label-free 3D imaging and analysis of live cells and organoids, leveraging digital holographic tomography and advanced computational reconstruction techniques.

results.title: New Source Performance Standards for Greenhouse Gas ...
results.content: The presumptive standard of performance for low-load natural gas-fired and oil-fired affected EGUs are in units of lb CO2 /MMBtu. While the EPA does not expect that states will use the RULOF provisions to provide less stringent standards of performance for these sources because their BSER is based on uniform fuels, should a state do so, the standard of performance would be determined in units of lb CO2 /MMBtu. 40 CFR 60.24a(f)) requires that a standard of performance pursuant to consideration of RULOF be no less stringent than necessary to address the fundamental difference identified under 40 CFR 60.24a(e)). The EPA strives to base its analyses on the best available science and economics, consistent with its responsibilities, for example, under the Information Quality Act.
